answer: Proof of space limits Sybil attacks by requiring agents to bind cryptographic plots to persistent storage before connecting at the network wharf. To deploy an orchard of fake identities, an adversary incurs the verifiable cost of provisioning dedicated physical disk capacity rather than spinning up ephemeral nodes that flash and disappear like a comet. A critical limitation is that high initialization overhead and storage wear disproportionately exclude honest, low-resource edge agents.
